facts.statement: The genus Palvennia was named after PalVenn, the Friends of the Palaeontological Museum in Oslo, whose expedition discovered the type specimen.
facts.quote: It was named for PalVenn, the Friends of the Palaeontological Museum in Oslo, whose expedition led to the discovery of the type specimen.

facts.statement: Palvennia lived during the uppermost Jurassic in Central Spitsbergen, Norway.
facts.quote: Palvennia is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurian known from the uppermost Jurassic of Central Spitsbergen, Norway.

facts.statement: Palvennia was a medium-sized ichthyosaur that measured between 3 and 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Palvennia was a medium-sized ichthyosaur, measuring 3 - 4 m long.

facts.statement: Palvennia had an unusually short rostrum, approximately 0.6 times the skull length, similar to Ichthyosaurus breviceps.
facts.quote: It is unusual in having a very short rostrum (~0.6× the skull length), similar to Ichthyosaurus breviceps.

facts.statement: The skull features a very large orbit, approximately 0.34 times the skull length, though this measurement may be distorted by crushing.
facts.quote: Because of this, the orbit seems very large (0.34× the skull length), but this may be affected by crushing.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Palvennia were discovered in 2004 in Spitsbergen within the Agardhfjellet Formation and dated to the Middle Volgian.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles aparecieron en 2004 en Spitsbergen, en la Formación Agardhfjellet, y se ha datado en el Volgiano medio.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen (SVB 1451) preserves nearly complete anterior skeletal material and a skull.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo (SVB 1451) conserva un cuarto anterior del esqueleto y el cráneo casi completos.

facts.statement: Palvennia is classified within the family Ophthalmosauridae.
The parent group of Palvennia is Ophthalmosaurinae.
In 2019, there was a debate regarding Palvennia's classification; while some researchers synonymized it with Arthropterygius, others argued they were distinct enough to remain separate genera.
facts.quote: In 2019, Palvennia was synonymized with Arthropterygius, though maintained as a separate species, by Nikolay Zverkov and Natalya Prilepskaya, although this synonymy was objected to later that same year by Lene Delsett and colleagues, who maintained that they were sufficiently different to warrant separate genera.
